conviction_note: Mixed evidence around a single central risk. The Aug-10 guide cut ($600-625M revenue, $1.34-1.51 adj EPS) needs H2 revenue of ~$151-164M a quarter against Q2's $145.2M, with originations down 9% and the line-of-credit launch already slipped once. That points to another miss or cut. On the other side: the stock is a further ~25% below its post-print level and at its 52-week low, short interest nearly doubled from 2.4M to 4.3M shares (est. ~17% of float, 7.4 days to cover), the CEO bought on the open market through mid-September, and the nearest peer (Enova, Oct 22) printed improving credit. So the findings sum to only +0.6, p_up is 52 and abs_move 11 (the name's median reaction is 10.8% and the last print moved -24.9%). The scaled number is +0.44, close to the findings' +0.6 sum.
bar: FY2026 company guide from the Aug-10 release: revenue $600-625M, adj net income $115-130M, adj EPS $1.34-1.51 on ~86M diluted shares (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818502/000181850226000073/oppfi-reportsxsecondxqua.htm). With H1 at $297.1M revenue and $0.68 adj EPS, H2 implies ~$303-328M revenue (~$151-164M a quarter) and $0.66-0.83 adj EPS (~$0.33-0.42 a quarter). Q3 Street bar comes from one source only: Earnings Whispers search snippet shows $0.41 EPS and $156.34M revenue (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/OPFI). MarketBeat puts FY consensus at ~$1.40, the low end of the guide (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-oppfi-nyse-opfi-hits-new-52-week-low-heres-why-2026-10-05/). That implies ~$0.36 a quarter in H2, so the $0.41 Q3 figure may be stale. The quarterly bar is single-source and disputed, so findings that depend on it are capped small. print_vs_bar_pct is my revenue estimate of ~$150-151M against $156.3M.
positioning_check: Short interest (Equibles, FINRA settlements): 4,283,126 shares on 2026-10-15 with 7.40 days to cover, versus 4,315,928 on 09-30, 3,494,465 on 09-15, 3,536,519 on 08-14 and 2,404,774 on 07-31 (https://equibles.com/stocks/opfi/shortinterest). MarketBeat (2026-10-05) gives market cap ~$511M at $5.97 (~86M shares) and insiders owning 70.2%, so the float is roughly 25M and the short is roughly 17% of float. That float-based percentage is my estimate, not a published figure. Skew is not available: the option chain is unusable (ATM spread 100% of mid, total OI 626, put/call OI 0.35). ATM IV of 95.5% on the 24-day Nov-20 expiry, against 31% 20-day realised vol, implies a large event premium. Tape: spot $5.44, -10.5% over 20 days, -52% from the 52-week high, 0.4% above the 52-week low.

findings.finding: OppFi's FY2026 guide (cut on Aug 10 to $600-625M revenue and $1.34-1.51 adj EPS) needs H2 revenue of ~$151-164M a quarter, against Q2 revenue of $145.2M (+1.9% y/y). Q2 net originations were down 9.3% and retained originations down 14.1% after tightened underwriting. The line-of-credit product slipped from summer to a September launch, and I found no confirmation that it has launched. A shrinking receivables base points to Q3 revenue of roughly $148-152M, below the ~$156M single-source Q3 consensus and at or below the low end of the guide's run-rate, so a second guidance trim is a live risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last guidance cut (2026-08-10, Q2 miss of $0.33 vs ~$0.44-0.48 plus the FY cut) moved the stock -24.86%. The 2026-03-11 print moved -5.87%. Prints with raises in 2025 moved +10.8%, +11.75% and +13.41%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is ~25% below its post-print ~$7.2, and FY consensus sits at the low end of the guide (~$1.40). If a second cut were fully priced, I would expect the Q3 Street revenue figure to sit below $150M rather than at $156M. The aggregator Q3 numbers look stale against the cut guide.
findings.independence: The line-of-credit slip to September and the LOLA migration delay come from Q2 call summaries (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/oppfi-q2-earnings-call-highlights), which share the company as the source. I found no independent evidence on OppFi's own Q3 originations.

findings.finding: Short interest built into the print. It rose from 2.40M shares (Jul 31) to 4.28M (Oct 15), with 7.4 days to cover and ~$3M a day of turnover, on a float of roughly 25M (insiders own ~70%). On a name trading at ~3.6-4x the low end of its own EPS guide, a reaffirmed guide or a stabilising credit print would force covering.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print on this name had a comparable short build that I could check. The baseline's reactions are skewed large in both directions (+13.4 to -24.9).
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is the market's own bet. What is not priced is the squeeze mechanism if the print is merely 'not worse'. If the market expected that outcome, shorts would have been covering into the print, but they held flat at ~4.3M from 09-30 to 10-15.
findings.independence: MarketBeat's 70.2% insider ownership and ~$511M market cap (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-oppfi-nyse-opfi-hits-new-52-week-low-heres-why-2026-10-05/) give the float denominator.

findings.finding: The nearest listed peer, Enova, reported Q3 on Oct 22, after OppFi last spoke: originations +31% y/y to $2.6B, consolidated net charge-off ratio 8.1% vs 8.5% a year earlier, and credit described as strong. Consumer Portfolio Services (subprime auto, Q3) also showed an improved annualized NCO of 7.26% vs 8.01% and lower delinquencies. Both read against a consumer-credit deterioration story for the non-prime borrower in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: OppFi's Q2 charge-offs rose to 52.3% of average receivables annualized (vs 43.5%), and that print moved -24.9%. I have not checked how the stock reacted to past peer credit prints.
findings.why_not_priced: OPFI fell further after Oct 22 (5-day run-up -3.4%), which suggests the market is not transferring peer credit health to OppFi. If it were, OPFI would have bounced off its lows in the days after the Enova print.
findings.independence: This is a proxy. Enova serves a different mix (near-prime and SMB) with different underwriting, and OppFi tightened for its own reasons. CPS Q3 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000889609/000168316826008042/cps_ex9901.htm

findings.finding: CEO Todd Schwartz bought Class A stock on the open market almost daily from about Aug 12 to Sep 15, 2026: ~$25k purchases at $6.97-7.62, not under a 10b5-1 plan. MarketBeat counts 130,640 shares (~$0.94M) of insider buying over 90 days. CFO Pamela Johnson sold 8,650 shares (~$69k) on Sep 11 under a Form 144.
findings.why_not_priced: The Form 4s are public, and the stock fell ~25% after the buys. The buys are token-sized against a controlling holder with ~27M shares. They stopped mid-September, probably at the quarter blackout, so they tell us about the CEO's view of Q3 as of early September but not after.
findings.independence: CEO Form 4 for Aug 18 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000090514826003815/form4.xml). CFO Form 144 for Sep 11 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000195917326006888/primary_doc.xml) points the other way, at small size.

findings.finding: On Sep 15 OppFi drew $75M of a $100M four-year residual facility (agreement dated Aug 10; UMB agent, Sertoma Park lender) at 12.50%, rising to 13.50% after the BNC deal closes, with a 1.25% OID and 10% semi-annual amortization. The stated use is 'to support growth in finance receivables', working capital and general purposes. This follows the termination of the Gray Rock SPV line in Q2.
findings.why_not_priced: The facility is public but expensive. Whether it funds a Q4 receivables build (seasonal plus the line-of-credit launch) shows up only in Q3 originations and receivables, which the release will reveal. On the financing question: the stated use is receivables growth, but Q2 originations were -9% and nothing yet corroborates a ramp, so I signed it roughly zero, slightly positive because there is no covenant or going-concern signal.
findings.independence: Q2 release liquidity section: unrestricted cash $64.3M, total funding capacity ~$541.8M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818502/000181850226000073/oppfi-reportsxsecondxqua.htm).

findings.finding: The $130M BNCCORP / BNC National Bank acquisition (guided >25% accretive to 2027 adj EPS, closing guided for Q4 2026) has BNCC holder approval (Sep 17) but no OCC/Fed/FDIC approval that I could find. It faces a Senator Warren letter (Aug 14) urging the regulators to block it and a 120+ group coalition asking for hearings and denial. The release and call will update the timing. A slip out of Q4 would hit the 2027 accretion story, and an approval would be a positive surprise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The deal announcement came on 2026-04-29, between prints. The stock went from ~$9.0 on Apr 28 to ~$9.8 by Aug 4 per the 424B3.
findings.why_not_priced: The opposition is public. What the market cannot yet see is management's updated close timing. If a slip were priced, the 2027 accretion would be absent from the multiple, and at ~4x the low end of the 2026 guide it arguably already is. That is why this finding is sized small.
findings.independence: Coalition opposition (https://www.nclc.org/broad-coalition-opposes-195-apr-bank-charter-for-oppfi-which-seeks-to-make-payday-loans-in-every-state/). Sep 21 8-K Item 8.01 confirms regulatory approvals are still outstanding.

outside_window.finding: The actual OCC/Fed/FDIC decision on the BNC National Bank acquisition, guided to close in Q4 2026. Only the call commentary falls inside the window.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The deeply negative run-up (-52% from the high, at the 52-week low) and the rising short interest already price a weak print, so my main negative (another revenue miss or cut) runs with the tape and is partly priced, while the positives (squeeze, peer credit) cut against it. Net, I moved p_up only to 52.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar single-source and disputed: EW Q3 $0.41/$156.3M vs FY consensus ~$1.40 implying ~$0.36 a quarter): capped the revenue/guide-cut negative, which depends on that bar, at -2.0 -> -1.5
Rule 7 (crowded short, ~17% of float est., 7.4 days to cover): shrank that negative further, -1.5 -> -1.2

Rule 5 (unexplained drawdown is not a finding; peer data is a proxy): positioning finding trimmed +1.5 -> +1.0 because it rests on short build, not on the drawdown; Enova/CPS proxy trimmed +1.0 -> +0.7
Rule 4 (financing is a question): stated use is receivables growth, no corroborated ramp (Q2 originations -9%), no covenant or going-concern signal, so sized near zero, +0.3 -> +0.2
Insider buys trimmed +0.5 -> +0.4 because they are token-sized for a controlling holder and stopped mid-September (rule 3, own caveat reaches the number)
BNC regulatory finding left at -0.5; abs_move_pct and p_up unchanged (11, 52)
